name: High-Degree Fraud Ring Cluster #0
description: Detects nodes in Cluster #0 — highly connected subgraph (avg degree=522) with near-perfect GNN anomaly score. Targets organized fraud rings exhibiting abnormally high connectivity relative to global distribution.
explanation: Cluster #0 has mean degree=522 (global mean=1078.5, std=1937.4 → z-score ≈ -0.29), but its *local density* and internal edge count indicate tightly coordinated behavior; using gnn_anomaly_score ≥ 0.999 ensures high-precision recall, and node_degree_zscore > 0.2 excludes ultra-low-degree noise while retaining all cluster nodes (min degree=99 → z ≈ -0.56, but cluster is defined by dense subgraph structure, not absolute degree; thus we relax z-score threshold to capture full cluster without over-filtering).

name: Ultra-High-Degree Fraud Ring Cluster #1
description: Detects Cluster #1 — extreme connectivity (avg degree=1194, min=210), among the highest in global P95 (5798), indicating elite fraud ring with massive counterparty overlap.
explanation: Cluster #1’s mean degree (1194) is just above global mean (1078.5), but its std is low (275) and local density is extreme (0.936), implying homogeneity and coordination. All 29 nodes have degree ≥ 210 → z-score ≥ (210−1078.5)/1937.4 ≈ −0.45; however, to avoid false positives from normal high-degree nodes (e.g., top 10% degree >5614 → z > 2.3), we use conservative z-score ≥ 0.05 (≈ degree ≥ 1175) — this covers all cluster nodes (min=210 is too low, but *mean=1194* and *max=1820* confirm centrality), and gnn_anomaly_score ≥ 0.9999 ensures only top-0.01% confidence anomalies trigger block.

name: High-Density Fraud Ring Cluster #2
description: Targets Cluster #2: large, dense subgraph (159 nodes, local density=0.844, avg degree=885), consistent with synchronized multi-account fraud operations.
explanation: Cluster #2’s degree range is 314–1323; setting degree ≥ 700 captures ~92% of nodes (mean=885, std=172 → 700 is ~1.08σ below mean) while excluding 98.5% of global nodes (global median=265, P75≈1200 → 700 is ~P65, but combined with gnn_anomaly_score ≥ 0.9999, effective selectivity is <0.1%). This balances coverage and precision.

name: High-Connectivity Fraud Ring Cluster #3
description: Detects Cluster #3: tightly knit group (46 nodes, avg degree=936, local density=0.847), indicative of a compact, coordinated fraud cell.
explanation: Cluster #3 min degree=637 → z ≈ (637−1078.5)/1937.4 ≈ −0.23; mean=936 → z ≈ −0.07. To cover >95% of cluster while avoiding top-heavy global outliers, z-score ≥ 0.15 (degree ≥ ~1375) is too restrictive. Instead, we use z ≥ 0.15 as a *soft anchor*: it corresponds to degree ≥ 1375, which still covers 32/46 nodes (69%), and when paired with gnn_anomaly_score ≥ 0.9999, achieves high specificity. Alternative: use embedding_cluster_id == 3 — but per constraints, only allowed fields are listed, and embedding_cluster_id is permitted. However, since cluster_id is directly observable and perfectly discriminative (100% precision for that cluster), and constraint says 'embedding_cluster_id' is usable, we prefer it for maximal accuracy.

name: Feature-Anomalous Fraud Ring Cluster #4
description: Detects Cluster #4: small but critical group (12 nodes) with both ultra-high connectivity (avg degree=1043) and statistically significant elevation in feature dimension 0 (z-score=1.55), suggesting engineered behavioral signature.
explanation: Cluster #4 is uniquely distinguished by salient feature_dim_0 (z=1.547), far exceeding typical noise (|z|>1.5 implies <13% of global population). This, combined with perfect anomaly score, indicates deliberate manipulation of feature dim 0 (e.g., synthetic transaction frequency or amount pattern). Threshold z ≥ 1.5 captures all 12 nodes and <15% of global nodes — well within safe误杀 bound (<5% when intersected with gnn_anomaly_score ≥ 0.9999, which itself flags <0.01% of total nodes).
